pp:ec:2010:q1.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 1
pp:ec:2010:q1.question: The eigen values of a skew-symmetric matrix are

detailed_solution.markdown:
A skew-synnmetric matrix is a square matrix whose

transpose is equal to its negative value, i.e. $A^{\top}=-A$

The eigen values of a skew-symmetric matrix

alwavs come in pairs $\pm \lambda$ (except in

odd-dimensional case where there is an additional

unpaired 0 eigen value). For a real skew symmetric

matrix the non-zero eigen values are all pure

imaginary and thus are of the form $i \lambda_{1},-i \lambda_{1}, i \lambda_{2}$

$-i \lambda_{2}, \ldots$ where each of the $\lambda_{K}$ is real.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2010:q2.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ec:2010:q2.question: The trigonometric Fourier series for the waveform $f(t)$ shown below contains
options: only cosine terms and zero values for the dc components
only cosine terms and a positive value for the dc components
only cosine terms and a negative value for the dc components
only sine terms and a negative value for the dc components

detailed_solution.markdown:
since  f(t) is an even function, its trigonometric

Fourier series contains only cosine terms.

D.C. component,

$$\begin{aligned} A_{0} &=\frac{1}{T} \int_{-T / 2}^{T / 2} f(t) d t=\frac{2}{T} \int_{0}^{T / 2} f(t) d t \\ &=\frac{2}{T}\left[\int_{0}^{T / 4} A d t+\int_{T / 4}^{T / 2}(-2 A) d t\right] \\ &=\frac{2}{T}\left[\frac{A T}{4}-2 A\left(\frac{T}{2}-\frac{T}{4}\right)\right] \\ &=\frac{2}{T}\left[-\frac{A T}{4}\right]=-\frac{A}{2} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the trigonometric Fourier series for the

waveform f(t) contains only cosine terms and a

negative value for the dc component.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2010:q3.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ec:2010:q3.question: A function $n(x)$  satisfied the differential equation $\frac{ d^{2}n(x)}{dx^{2}}-\frac{n(x)}{L^{2}}=0$ where L is a constant. The boundary conditions are : $n(0) = K$ and $n(\infty )$ = 0. The solution to this equation is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \left(D^{2}-\frac{1}{L^{2}}\right) n(x) &=0 \\ D^{2}-\frac{1}{L^{2}} &=0 \\ D &=\pm \frac{1}{L} \end{aligned}$$

So, the solution is

$$\begin{aligned} n(x) &=C_{1} e^{x / L}+C_{2} e^{-x / L} \\ n(0) &=K \Rightarrow C_{1}+C_{2}=K \\ n(\infty) &=0 \Rightarrow C_{1}=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad C_{2} &=K \\ \text { Therefore, } n(x) &=K \exp (-x / L) \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

detailed_solution.markdown: Short-circuit admittance parameters for a two-port $\pi$-network are, $$\begin{array}{l} Y_{11}=Y_{a}+Y_{b} \\ Y_{12}=Y_{21}=-Y_{b} \\ Y_{22}=Y_{b}+Y_{c} \end{array}$$ For the given network, $$\begin{aligned} Y_{a}&=Y_{b}=Y_{c}=\frac{1}{0.5}=2 \mho\\ \text{So,}Y_{11}&=2+2=4 \mho\\ Y_{12}&=Y_{21}=-2 \mho\\ Y_{22}&=2+2=4 \mho \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ec:2010:q5.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 5
pp:ec:2010:q5.question: For parallel RLC circuit, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: The bandwidth of the circuit decreases if R is increased
The bandwidth of the circuit remains same if L is increased
At resonance, input impedance is a real quantity
At resonance, the magnitude of input impedance attains its minimum values

detailed_solution.concept: Network Theory - Sinusoidal Steady State Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown:
Characteristic equation for a parallel RLC circuit is

$s^{2}+\frac{1}{R C} s+\frac{1}{L C}=0$

where, Bandwidth= $\frac{1}{RC}$

(i) It is clear that the bandwidth of a parallel RLC

circuit is independent of L and decreases if

R is increased.

(ii) At resonance, imaginary part of input

impedance is zero. Hence, at resonance input

impedance is a real quantity.

(iii) In parallel RLC circuit, the admittance is

minimum at resonance. Hence magnitude of

input impedance attains its maximum value

at resonance.

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2010:q15.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 15
pp:ec:2010:q15.question: Two discrete time system with impulse response $h_{1}[n]=\delta [n-1]$ and $h_{2}[n]=\delta [n-2]$ are connected in cascade. The overall impulse response of the cascaded system is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} h_{1}[n]&=\delta[n-1] \stackrel{Z}{\longleftrightarrow} H_{1}(z)=z^{1} \\ h_{2}[n]&=\delta[n-2] \stackrel{Z}{\longleftrightarrow} H_{2}(z)=z^{2} \end{aligned}$$

Overall impulse response in z-domain,

$$\begin{aligned} H(z) &=H_{1}(z) H_{2}(z) \\ &=z^{-1} z^{-2} \\ &=z^{-3} \end{aligned}$$

Overall impulse response in discrete-time domain.

$h[n]=\delta(n-3)$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

From the transfer function,

pp:ec:2010:q20.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 20
pp:ec:2010:q20.question: Suppose that the modulating signal is $m(t)=2cos(2\pi f_{m}t)$ and the carrier signal is $X_{c}(t)=A_{c}cos(2\pi f_{c}t)$, which one of the following is a conventional AM signal without over-modulation

detailed_solution.markdown:
Conventional AM signal is

$$\begin{aligned} x(t) &=A_{c}[1+m(t)] \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right) \\ &=A_{c} \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)+A_{c} m(t) \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right) \end{aligned}$$

In option (B),

Modulation index $=\frac{2}{1}=2$

So, it is conventional AM signal but with overmodulation.

In option (C)

$x(t)=A_{c} \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)+\frac{A_{c}}{4} m(t) \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)$

Here,Modulation index

$=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$

Therefore, it is conventional AM signal without over-modulation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2010:q23.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 23
pp:ec:2010:q23.question: A transmission line has a characteristic impedance of 50 $\Omega$ and a resistance of 0.1$\Omega$/m . If the line is distortion less, the attenuation constant(in Np/m) is

detailed_solution.markdown:
For distortionless transmission line,

$$\begin{aligned} L G&=R C \\ \Rightarrow \frac{L}{C}&=\frac{R}{G} \end{aligned}$$

Characteristic impedance,

$Z_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}=\sqrt{\frac{R}{G}}$

Attenuation constant,

$$\begin{aligned} \alpha &=\sqrt{R G}=\sqrt{R} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{R}}{Z_{0}}=\frac{R}{Z_{0}}=\frac{0.1}{50} \\ &=0.002 \mathrm{Np} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2010:q25.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 25

relative permittivity of the medium is 4, the magnitude of the time-average

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2010:q27.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 27
pp:ec:2010:q27.question:
A fair coin is tossed independently four times. The probability of the event "the
number of time heads shown up is more than the number of times tail shown up"

detailed_solution.markdown:
The only 5 events when the number of times of

heads show up is more than the number of times

tails show up are given below:

$$\begin{array}{cccc} H&H&H&H\\ H&H&H&T\\ H&H&T&H\\ H&T&H&H\\ T&H&H&H \end{array}$$

since fair coin is tossed independently four times,

the probability of each above events is

$\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{16}$

All above events are mutually exclusive, so, total

probability

$=\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{16}=\frac{5}{16}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2010:q28.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ec:2010:q28.question: If $\vec{A}=xy\hat{a}_{x}+x^{2}\hat{a}_{y}$, then $\oint_{0}^{C}\vec{A}\cdot \vec{dl}$ over the path shown in the figure is

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \vec{A} &=x y \hat{a}_{x}+x^{2} \hat{a}_{y} \\ \vec{l} &=x \hat{a}_{x}+y \hat{a}_{y} \\ \vec{d} t &=d x \hat{a}_{x}+d y \hat{a}_{y} \\ \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} t &=x y d x+x^{2} d y \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} P-Q&\\ y&=1,dy=0\\ \int_{P}^{0} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} i &=\int_{1 / \sqrt{3}}^{2 / \sqrt{3}} x d x=\left.\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right|_{1 / \sqrt{3}} ^{2 / \sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{2} \\ Q-R: &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}, d x=0 \\ \int_{0}^{R} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} t &=\int_{1}^{3}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^{2} d y=\frac{4}{3}(3-1)=\frac{8}{3}\\ R-S: & \\ y&=3, d y=0 \\ \int_{A}^{S} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} t &=\int_{2 / \sqrt{3}}^{1 / \sqrt{3}} 3 x d x=\left.\frac{3}{2} x^{2}\right|_{2 / \sqrt{3}} ^{\sqrt{3}} \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{4}{3}\right)=\frac{-3}{2} \\ S-P & \\ x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}, & d x=0 \\ \int_{S}^{P} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} i &=\int_{3}^{1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^{2} d y=\frac{1}{3}(1-3)=\frac{-2}{3} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \text { So, } \oint_{C} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} \vec{l}=& \int_{P}^{Q} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} \vec{t}+\int_{Q}^{R} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d}+\int_{R}^{S} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d}+\int_{S}^{P} \vec{A} \cdot \vec{d} \\ &=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{8}{3}-\frac{3}{2}-\frac{2}{3}=1 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2010:q29.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 29
pp:ec:2010:q29.question: The residues of a complex function $X(z)=\frac{1-2z}{z(z-1)(z-2)}$ at its poles are

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given that,

$$\begin{aligned} X(z)&=\frac{1-2 z}{z(z-1)(z-2)} \\ \text{Res}(0)&=\lim _{z \rightarrow 0} 1 \cdot\left[\frac{1-2 z}{(z-1)(z-2)}\right]=\frac{1}{2} \\ \text{Res}(1)&=\lim _{z \rightarrow 1} 1 \cdot\left[\frac{1-2 z}{z(z-2)}\right]=\frac{-1}{1(-1)}=1 \\ \text{Res}(2)&=\lim _{z \rightarrow 2} 1 \cdot\left[\frac{1-2 z}{z(z-1)}\right] \\ &=\frac{1-4}{2(2-1)}=\frac{-3}{2} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2010:q31.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 31
pp:ec:2010:q31.question: Given $f(t)=l^{-1}[\frac{3s+1}{s^{3}+4s^{2}+(K-3)s}].$ If $\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty }f(t)=1$, then the value of K is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} f(t)=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} s F(s)$

Given that,

$$\begin{array}{l} \quad F(s)=\left[\frac{3 s+1}{s^{3}+4 s^{2}+(K-3) s}\right] \\ \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} f(t)=1 \\ \Rightarrow \lim _{s \rightarrow 0} s\left[\frac{3 s+1}{s^{3}+4 s^{2}+(K-3) s}\right]=1 \\ \Rightarrow \lim _{s \rightarrow 0}\left[\frac{3 s+1}{s^{2}+4 s+(K-3)}\right]=1 \\ \Rightarrow \frac{1}{K-3}=1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad k-3=1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad K=4 \\ \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2010:q32.question: In the circuit shown, the switch S is open for a long time and is closed at $t=0$. The current $i(t)$ for $t\geq 0^{+}$ is

detailed_solution.markdown: Method 1: At $t = 0^{-}$. the circuit is shown below: Current will divide equally in both $10\Omega$ resistors as shown in diagram. At $t\geq 0^{+}$, the circuit ins-domain is shown below: $[L = 15 mH, i(O+) = i(O^{-}) = 0.75 A]$ The above circuit can be rearranged as given below: Applying nodal analysis, $$\begin{aligned} &\frac{V(s)-\frac{1.5}{s}}{10}+\frac{V(s)}{10}+\frac{V(s)+15 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.75}{10+15 \times 10^{-3} s}=0 \\ &\frac{\frac{V(s)}{10}+\frac{V(s)}{10}+\frac{V(s)}{10+15 \times 10^{-3} s}}{10 s}-\frac{15 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.75}{10+15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}} \\ &=\frac{15}{10}\left[\frac{10+15 \times 10^{-3} s+5}{5\left(10+15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}\right)}\right]\\ & \text { V(s) }\left[\frac{10+15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}+5}{5\left(10+15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}\right)}\right] \\ =& 15\left[\frac{10+15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}-10 \mathrm{s} \times 10^{-3} \times 0.75}{10\left(10+15 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}\right)}\right] \\ & \text { (1 }\left.+10^{-3} \mathrm{s}\right) V(s)=\frac{\left(10+7.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{s}\right)}{2 s}\left[\frac{s+1000}{1000}\right] \\ &V(s) =\frac{10000+7.5 \mathrm{s}}{2000 \mathrm{s}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{array}{l} V(s)=\frac{10000+7.5 s}{2 s(s+1000)} \\ =\frac{10000}{2 \times 1000 s}+\frac{\{10000+7.5(-1000)\}}{2(-1000)(s+1000)} \\ =\frac{5}{s}-\frac{1.25}{s+1000} \end{array}$$ Taking inverse Laplace transform, $$\begin{aligned} v(t)&=5-1.25 e^{-1000 t} \mathrm{V}\\ i(t) &=\frac{v(t)}{10} \\ &=0.5-0.125 e^{-1000 t} \mathrm{A} \end{aligned}$$ Method 2: $$\begin{aligned} i\left(0^{+}\right)&=\frac{0.75}{2}=0.375 \mathrm{A}\\ i(\infty) &=0.5 \mathrm{A} \\ i(t) &=i(\infty)-\left\{i(\infty)-i\left(0^{+}\right)\right\} e^{-R t L} \end{aligned}$$ where, R = equivalent resistance seen across L with current source opened $$\begin{aligned} R &=10+(10 \| 10)=15 \Omega \\ i(t) &=0.5-\{0.5-0.375\} e^{-15 t 15 \times 10^{-3}} \\ &=0.5-0.125 e^{-1000 t} \mathrm{A} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ec:2010:q41.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:ec:2010:q41.question:
A continuous time LTI system is described by $\frac{d^{2}y(t)}{dt^{2}}+4\frac{dy(t)}{dt}+3y(t)=2\frac{dx(t)}{dt}+4x(t)$
Assuming zero initial conditions, the response y(t) of the above system for the input $x(t)=e^{-2t}u(t)$ is given by

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{d^{2} y(t)}{d t^{2}}+\frac{4 d y(t)}{d t}+3 y(t)=\frac{2 d x(t)}{d t}+4 x(t)$

Taking Laplace transform on both sides (assuming

zero initial conditions).

$$\begin{aligned} s^{2} Y(s)+4 s Y(s)+3 Y(s)&=2 s X(s)+4 X(s) \\ \text{or }\quad \frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}&=\frac{2 s+4}{s^{2}+4 s+3} \\ &=\frac{2(s+2)}{(s+1)(s+3)} \end{aligned}$$

Given that

$$\begin{aligned} x(t) &=e^{2 t} u(t) \\ x(s) &=\frac{1}{s+2} \\ Y(s) &=\frac{2(s+2)}{(s+1)(s+3)(s+2)} \\ &=\frac{2}{(s+1)(s+3)} \\ &=\frac{1}{s+1}-\frac{1}{s+3} \end{aligned}$$

Taking inverse Laplace transform on both sides.

$y(t)=(e^{-t}-e^{-3t})u(t)$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ec:2010:q42.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 42
pp:ec:2010:q42.question:
The transfer function of a discrete time LTI system is given by
$H(z)=\frac{2-\frac{3}{4}z^{-1}}{1-\frac{3}{4}z^{-1}+\frac{1}{8}z^{-2}}$
Consider the following statements:
S1: The system is stable and causal for ROC: |z| $\gt$ 1/2
S2: The system is stable but not causal for ROC:| z| $\lt$ 1/4
S3: The system is neither stable nor causal for ROC: 1/4 $\lt$ |z| $\lt$ 1/2
Which one of the following statements is valid ?
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
Both S2 and S3 are true
Both S1 and S3 are true
S1, S2 and S3 are all

detailed_solution.markdown:
A discrete-time LTI system is causal if and

only if the ROC of its system function is the

exterior of a circle, including infinity.

A discrete-time LTI system is stable if and only

if the ROC of its system function includes the

unit circle,  $|z|=1$

$$H(z)=\begin{array}{l}\left(1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}\right)+\left(1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}\right) \\ \left(1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}\right)\end{array}$$

or  $H(z)=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{4} z^{-1}}+\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{2} z^{-1}}$

For  $\mathrm{ROC}:|z| \gt \frac{1}{2},$

the system is stable and

causal.

For  $\mathrm{ROC}:|z| \lt \frac{1}{4},$

ROC  does not include unit

circle. So, system is not stable.

For  $ROC: \frac{1}{4} \lt |z| \lt \frac{1}{2},$

ROC  does not include

unit circle. So, system is not stable.

Also ROC  is not the exterior of  $|z|=\frac{1}{2}$ .So,  it is not causal.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ec:2010:q44.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 44
pp:ec:2010:q44.question:
A unity negative feedback closed loop system has a plant with the transfer function $G(s)=\frac{1}{s^{2}+2s+2}$ and a controller $G_{c}(s)$ in the
feed forward path. For a unit set input, the transfer function of the controller that
gives minimum steady state error is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Steady state error,

$$\begin{aligned} e_{s s} &=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} \frac{s R(s)}{1+G(s) G_{c}(s)} \\ r(t) &=u(t) \\ R(s) &=\frac{1}{s} \\ e_{ss} &=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} \frac{s \cdot \frac{1}{s}}{1+G(s) G_{c}(s)} \\ e_{ss}&=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} \frac{1}{1+G(s) G_{c}(s)} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad G_{c}(s) &=\frac{s+1}{s+2}, e_{s s}=\frac{2}{3} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad G_{c}(s) &=\frac{s+2}{s+1}, e_{s s}=\frac{1}{3} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad G_{c}(s) &=\frac{(s+1)(s+4)}{(s+2)(s+3)}, e_{s s}=\frac{3}{5} \\ \text { Taking, } \quad & G_{c}(s)=1+\frac{2}{s}+3 s, e_{s s}=0 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2010:q45.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 45
pp:ec:2010:q45.question:
X(t) is a stationary process with the power spectral density $S_{x}(f) \gt 0$, for all f. The process is passed through a system shown below

Let $S_{y}(f)$ be the power spectral density of Y(t). Which one of the following statements is correct
options: $S_{y}(f)$ = 0 for $f = nf_{0} , f_{0} = 2 kHz$, n any integer
$S_{y}(f)$ = 0 for $f =(2n+1), f_{0} = 1 kHz$,  n any integer

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} y_{1}(t) &=x(t)+x\left(t-0.5 \times 10^{-3}\right) \\ Y_{1}(f) &=X(f)\left[1+e^{-j 2 \pi t\left(0.5 \times 10^{-3}\right)}\right] \\ H_{1}(f) &=\gamma_{X(f)}=1+e^{-j \pi f \times 10^{-3}} \\ H(f) &=H_{1}(f) \cdot H_{2}(f) \\ &=(j 2 \pi f)\left[1+e^{-j\left(\pi t \times 10^{-3}\right)}\right] \\ H(f)^{2} &=4 \pi^{2} f^{2}\left[2+2 \cos \left(\pi f \times 10^{-3}\right)\right] \\ &=8 \pi^{2} f^{2}\left[1+\cos \left(\pi f \times 10^{-3}\right)\right] \\ S_{y}(f) &=|H(f)|^{2} S_{x}(f) \\ &=8 \pi^{2} f^{2}\left[1+\cos \left(\pi f \times 10^{-3}\right)\right] S_{x}(f)\\ \text{For}\quad f &=(2n+1)f_{o};\text{ with }f_{o}=1KHz \end{aligned}$$ $\pi f \times 10^{-3}$ is an odd multiple of $\pi$ $\therefore S_{y}(f)=0$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ec:2010:q47.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 47
pp:ec:2010:q47.question: In the circuit shown, all the transmission line sections are lossless. The Voltage Standing Wave Ration(VSWR) on the 60 $\Omega$ line is

detailed_solution.markdown: $Z_{\text {in }}=Z_{0}\left(\frac{Z_{L}+j Z_{0} \tan \beta l}{Z_{0}+j Z_{L} \tan \beta l}\right)$ Input impedance, $$\begin{aligned} Z_{1} &=30\left[\frac{0+j 30 \tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\right)\left(\frac{\lambda}{8}\right)}{30+0}\right] \\ \Rightarrow Z_{1} &=j 30 \\ Z_{2} &=30 \sqrt{2}\left[\frac{30+j 30 \sqrt{2} \tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\right)\left(\frac{\lambda}{4}\right)}{30 \sqrt{2}+j 30 \tan \left(\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\right)\left(\frac{\lambda}{4}\right)}\right] \\ &=30 \sqrt{2}\left[\frac{\frac{30}{\tan \pi / 2}+j 30 \sqrt{2}}{\frac{30 \sqrt{2}}{\tan \pi / 2}+j 30}\right] \\ &=60 \Omega \\ \text { or, } Z_{2}&=\frac{(30 \sqrt{2})^{2}}{30}=60 \Omega & \end{aligned}$$ Load impedance, $Z_{L}=Z_{1}+Z_{2}=j 30+6$ Magnitude of reflection coefficient, $$\begin{aligned} |\Gamma|&=\left|\frac{Z_{L}-Z_{0}}{Z_{L}+Z_{0}}\right|=\left|\frac{60+j 30-60}{60+j 30+60}\right|\\ &=\left|\frac{j 30}{120+j 30}\right|=\mid \frac{j 1}{4+j \mid} \\ &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{16+1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}} \end{aligned}$$ VSWR on 60 \Omega line, $\text { VSWR }=\frac{1+|\Gamma|}{1-|\Gamma|}=\frac{1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}}{1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}}=1.64$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ec:2010:q51.question:

detailed_solution.markdown:
Forward path gain,

$$\begin{aligned} P_{1} &=2\left(\frac{1}{s}\right)\left(\frac{1}{s}\right)(0.5)=\frac{1}{s^{2}} \\ P_{2} &=2\left(\frac{1}{s}\right)(1)(0.5)=\frac{1}{s} \\ \Delta_{1} &=1 \\ \Delta_{2} &=1 \\ \Delta &=1-\left\{-\frac{1}{s}-\frac{1}{s^{2}}\right\} \\ &=1+\frac{1}{s}+\frac{1}{s^{2}} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2010:q53.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 53
pp:ec:2010:q53.question:
The silicon sample with unit cross-sectional area shown below is in thermal equilibrium. The following information is given: T = 300 K electronic charge=$1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C, thermal voltage = 26 mV and electron mobility = $1350 cm^{2}$/V-s

The magnitude of the electron of the electron drift current density at $x=0.5 \mu m$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{array}{l} J=\sigma E \quad\sigma=nq\mu_{n}=N_{D}q\mu_{n}\\ J=N_{D} q \mu_{n} E \\ J=10^{16} \times\left(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\right)(1350)\left(10 \times 10^{3}\right) \\ J=2.16 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{A} / \mathrm{cm}^{2} \end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ec:2010:q54.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 54

detailed_solution.markdown: Output noise power $=|H(f)|^{2} \cdot$ (input noise PSD) $\mathcal{S}_{\text{NO}}(F)=S_{N}(f)|H(f)|^{2}$ $\mathcal{S}_{\text{NO}}(f)=10^{-20}|H(f)|^{2}$ Output noise power $=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} S_{\text {NO }}(f) d f$ $=10^{-20} \frac{\mathrm{W}}{\mathrm{Hz}} \times 2 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{Hz}$ $=2 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{W}$ since mean square value = power $\frac{2}{\alpha^{2}}=2 \times 10^{-14} \rightarrow \alpha=10^{7}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ec:2010:q55.title: GATE EC 2010 | Set 1 | Question: 55

detailed_solution.markdown:
When a '1' is transmitted:

$$\begin{array}{l} Y_{K}=a+N_{K} \\ \text { Threshold } Z=\frac{a}{2}=10^{-6} \\ a=2 \times 10^{-6} \end{array}$$

For error to occur, $Y_{K} \lt 10^{-6}$

$$\begin{aligned} 2 \times 10^{-6}&+N_{K}\lt 10^{-6} \\ N_{K} & \lt -10^{-6} \\ P(0 / 1) &=\int_{-\infty}^{-10^{-6}} P_{N K}(n) d n \\ &=\int_{-\infty}^{-10^{-6}} 0.5 \alpha e^{\alpha n} d n \text { with } \alpha=10^{7} \\ P(0 / 1) &=0.5 e^{-10} \end{aligned}$$

When a '0' is transmitted:

$Y_{K}=N_{K}$

For error to occur, $Y_{K} \gt 10^{-6}$

$\therefore \; P(1 / 0)=\int_{10^{-6}}^{\infty} P_{N K}(n) d n=0.5 \times e^{-10}$

since, both bits are equiprobable;

$P(0)=P(1)=\frac{1}{2}$

the probability of bit error

$=P(1) \cdot P(0 / 1)+P(0) \cdot P(1 / 0)$

$=\frac{P(0 / 1)+P(1 / 0)}{2}=0.5 \times

e^{-10}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.
